lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: understand the general structure of the circulation system, including the blood vessels to and from the heart and lungs, liver and kidneys

primer.text: Your blood travels a one-way loop through a closed network of vessels, stopping at the lungs to collect oxygen and at the liver and kidneys to deliver and collect. This note maps the whole circuit and the named vessels that feed each organ, including the two famous exceptions.

modules.title: The Circulation and Its Named Vessels
sourceHeadings: Main Blood Vessels of the Circulatory System Table
modules.opening: Blood flows one way around a closed network: arteries carry it outward from the heart, capillaries trade with the organs, and veins gather it back, with the pulmonary pair forming the famous exception pair.
keyPoints: Arteries usually carry oxygenated blood away from the heart.
The pulmonary artery is the exception, taking deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
The pulmonary vein returns freshly oxygenated blood, the reverse exception.
Arteries narrow into arterioles, then capillaries, then widen into venules and veins.
Lymphatic vessels return leaked tissue fluid to the circulation.

low.restatement: Outward arteries, returning veins, one-way flow, and the pulmonary pair breaking the oxygen rule.
low.analogy: A delivery van loop: outbound on the motorway, doorstep stops, then the return lane home.
low.examPointer: Learn the vessel table: vena cava and pulmonary vein in; aorta and pulmonary artery out.

medium.restatement: Each organ has its own in-pair and out-pair — hepatic artery plus portal vein for the liver, renal artery and vein for the kidneys — all wired into the one-way loop.
medium.analogy: A ring road with private driveways: every house (organ) has its own entrance and exit onto the same circuit.
medium.examPointer: Practise writing the liver row in full: hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein toward it, hepatic vein away.

glossary.definition: The artery carrying deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
The vein bringing oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
The vein carrying digested food from the gut toward the liver.
Drainage vessels returning leaked tissue fluid to the circulation.

figures.alt: Diagram of the circulatory system showing blood flow between the heart, lungs, liver, gut, kidneys, and other organs with labelled veins and arteries.
